question.problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.$*
question.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,{x}^{2}\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le x\}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{0}^{x}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14248203/assets/96ac5800a3c28448548ae60889724f82961312232ea27f1cf1233788e6a1d259.png)

The region $D$ is type I region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{2}\le z\le 1\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
x=0
$$

and the right boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(z),$ is

$$
z={x}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{z}.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{z}\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14248203/assets/3c108855dfd47c0917ee72fc6360fb0696538165c7f960903fd8c33d38be6ed5.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{z}}{\int }_{0}^{x}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{z}}[{\int }_{0}^{x}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})\text{d}y]\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{z}}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})[y]_{0}^{x}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{z}}4x\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{z}}2x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})[{x}^{2}]_{0}^{\sqrt{z}}\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2z\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})\,\text{d}z \\  & ={[-\operatorname{cos}⁡({z}^{2})]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-(\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)-1) \\  & =1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(1).\end{aligned}
$$
